# SB-1025 Safety bulletin: quench oil fire risk

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P1, line P1-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L1-RR01

Hazard description
- Overview: Recent inspections and incident trend analysis identify an elevated quench oil fire risk associated with the radial ring rolling mill identified as EQ-P1-L1-RR01. The primary mechanism is oil ingress to the hot work zone followed by contact with heated surfaces and ignition. Contributing factors include oil leaks, excessive oil carryover from roll surfaces, degraded oil quality, and inadequate housekeeping in the quench and transfer zones.
- Failure modes: Oil that accumulates on machine housings, guards, or roll surfaces can reach ignition temperature when exposed to hot billets, frictional heating, or nearby radiant heat sources. Restricted drain paths or contaminated sump screens allow oil to pool near heat sources. Inadequate ventilation increases local temperature and delays dispersion of vapors.
- Consequences: Fire involving quench oil can rapidly spread to adjacent equipment, compromise structural guards, and endanger personnel during shift change or maintenance activities. Secondary risks include smoke inhalation, loss of process capability, and extended downtime while fire damage is remediated.

Affected equipment
- Scope: The controls in this bulletin apply to EQ-P1-L1-RR01 located in Plant P1, line P1-L1. Referenced maintenance and operating procedures for this equipment are MM-P1-L1-RR01, SOP-P1-L1-04, and SOP-P1-L1-05.
- Components of concern: Quench tank(s), quench oil delivery lines, roll housings, bearings adjacent to the quench zone, transfer conveyors, splash shields, and local ventilation systems. The main roll bearing lubrication interval for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill EQ-P1-L1-RR01 is 120 hours. Lubrication practices that permit excess oil to escape toward the quench zone are a primary focus.
- Past observations: Inspections revealed oil wicking along bearing seals into lower housings and oil film on roll collars that transfers to the quench area during loading. Housekeeping records show accumulation of oily rags and dust in vicinity of the quench tank at several recent walkdowns; refer to MM-P1-L1-RR01 for inspection checklists.

Required controls
- Immediate controls (apply immediately): 
  - Stopwork rule in the quench area if visible oil pooling or active oil leaks are observed. Personnel must notify supervision and tag equipment out until corrected.
  - Increase frequency of visual inspection for oil carryover along roll collars and housings during shift turnover and before hot work. Use the inspection checklist in MM-P1-L1-RR01 to document condition and actions taken.
- Engineering and administrative controls:
  - Implement oil containment and drainage improvements to prevent pooling near hot zones. Ensure drain paths lead to closed sumps and are free of debris; use the containment guidance in SOP-P1-L1-04.
  - Apply drip shields or splash guards on bearing housings and delivery lines to deflect stray oil away from hot surfaces. Maintain shields per SOP-P1-L1-05.
  - Review lubrication practices that result in excess oil application. For EQ-P1-L1-RR01, adhere to the specified main roll bearing lubrication interval of 120 hours and follow the lubrication steps in MM-P1-L1-RR01 to avoid over-application.
  - Control ignition sources by enforcing hot surface clearance and restricting hot work permits in adjacent zones. Coordinate with the permit issuing authority per SOP-P1-L1-04.
  - Ensure ventilation in the quench zone is operating nominally and filters or ducts are not clogged; include ventilation checks in the pre-shift inspection list.
- Training and PPE:
  - Conduct targeted toolbox talks for operators and maintenance staff on recognizing early signs of oil migration and safe isolation of quench oil systems. Include examples drawn from MM-P1-L1-RR01.
  - Ensure fire-resistant PPE and appropriate extinguishing equipment for oil fires are available at designated stations and that staff are trained in their use in accordance with site procedures.
- Monitoring and verification:
  - Use the inspection and repair log in MM-P1-L1-RR01 to record leak discovery, corrective actions, and verification checks. Entries must include observed condition, corrective action taken, and name of individual performing the work.
  - Maintenance planning must incorporate adherence to the 120 hours lubrication interval. Scheduling records shall reference MM-P1-L1-RR01 and be available for audit.
  - Conduct a focused safety audit after implementation of controls and again at regular intervals to verify effectiveness as described in SOP-P1-L1-05.

Background and step rationale
- Why controls are required: Quench oils are hydrocarbon-based and present a flammable liquid hazard when placed in contact with hot surfaces or dispersed as vapor in confined hot zones. Preventing oil migration and accumulation is more effective than relying solely on fire response, because prevention reduces probability of ignition and scope of exposure.
- Rationale for lubrication interval emphasis: Ensuring the main roll bearings on EQ-P1-L1-RR01 follow the documented lubrication interval of 120 hours and proper application technique reduces the likelihood of over-lubrication that can lead to oil escape into the quench zone. Corrective action focuses on technique, containment, and inspection rather than arbitrary increases in lubrication frequency.

Examples and practical notes
- Example inspection entry: "Quench sump screen cleared; small oil film on lower roll collar observed; applied containment shield and wiped film per SOP-P1-L1-05; notified maintenance and scheduled bearing lubrication per MM-P1-L1-RR01."
- Example corrective action: Temporary drip shield installed and oil supply line clamp replaced; leak sealed and area cleaned using absorbents; repair recorded in MM-P1-L1-RR01.
- Avoid using loose rags for oil cleanup. Place used absorbents in sealed containers and dispose per waste handling procedure referenced in MM-P1-L1-RR01.

Records to keep
- Inspection logs maintained under MM-P1-L1-RR01 documenting pre-shift checks, discovery of oil accumulation, and corrective actions.
- Lubrication schedule and service records showing adherence to the 120 hours interval for the main roll bearing on EQ-P1-L1-RR01.
- Training attendance records and toolbox talk sign-in sheets referencing SOP-P1-L1-04 and SOP-P1-L1-05.
- Repair and audit reports demonstrating completion of engineering controls and verification checks; retain records in the equipment file for EQ-P1-L1-RR01.

Effective date
- Effective: immediately upon issuance of this bulletin. All affected personnel shall implement the required controls without delay and document actions in the records specified above.
